message.content:
**Uno – Quick Overview** | Item | Details | |------|---------| | **Deck** | 108 cards (4 colors × 25 cards + 8 special cards) | | **Goal** | Be the first player to score 500 points (or play all cards in a single round). | | **Setup** | Shuffle the deck and deal 7 cards to each player. Place the remaining cards face‑down as the draw pile; flip the top card to start the discard pile. | | **Turn Sequence** | 1️⃣ Draw a card from the draw pile if you cannot or choose not to play.
2️⃣ Play one card that matches either color, number, or symbol of the top discard.
3️⃣ If you have no playable card, you may play a “Draw Two” or “Wild Draw Four” only if you have no matching color/number cards (see rule 5). | | **Special Cards** | • **Skip** – next player loses a turn.
• **Reverse** – changes direction of play.
• **Draw Two** – next player draws two cards and skips a turn.
• **Wild** – you choose the new color.
• **Wild Draw Four** – you choose the new color; next player draws four cards and skips a turn (must be played only when you have no other playable card). | | **Winning a Round** | When a player discards their last card, they earn points equal to the sum of the values of all cards left in opponents’ hands. | | **Scoring** | 0–9 = face value, 10–12 = 20 points, 13–15 = 50 points. | | **Winning the Game** | First player to reach 500 points (or agreed target) wins. | **Key Rules & Tips** | Rule | Explanation | |------|-------------| | **Rule 1 – Matching** | A card can be played if it shares the same color, number, or symbol with the top discard. | | **Rule 2 – Wilds** | Wild cards can be played at any time; you announce the new color. | | **Rule 3 – “Draw Two” & “Wild Draw Four”** | These cards force the next player to draw cards and skip a turn. | | **Rule 4 – “Uno” Call** | When you have one card left, shout “UNO!” before your opponent takes their turn. Failure to call results in a penalty (draw two cards). | | **Rule 5 – Challenge** | If a “Wild Draw Four” is played, the next player may challenge. If the challenger has a playable card of the declared color, the challenger draws four cards; otherwise the challenger draws six cards. | | **Rule 6 – Turn Order** | Reverse changes the direction of play; Skip causes the next player to lose a turn. | | **Rule 7 – Deck Replenishment** | When the draw pile runs out, shuffle the discard pile (except the top card) to form a new draw pile. | | **Rule 8 – Winning a Round** | Points are tallied after each round; the winner of the round gets the points. | | **Rule 9 – Game End** | The game ends when a player reaches the target score (e.g., 500). | | **Rule 10 – Variations** | Many house rules exist (e.g., “Stacking” where players stack Draw Twos). Clarify before starting. | **Common House Rules (Optional)** | Variation | Description | |-----------|-------------| | **Stacking** | Players may stack “Draw Two” or “Wild Draw Four” on top of each other, forcing the next player to draw the cumulative total. | | **No Challenge** | Some groups never challenge “Wild Draw Four.” | | **Penalty for Not Calling UNO** | Instead of drawing two cards, the player who fails to call may lose a turn. | | **Custom Point Target** | Players may agree on a lower target (e.g., 200 points) for shorter games. | **Quick Play Summary** 1. Deal 7 cards each. Flip top card to start discard pile. 2. Player to the left goes first. 3. On your turn, play a matching card or draw if you cannot. 4. Use special cards strategically. 5. Call “UNO” when you’re down to one card. 6. Finish the round when someone discards all cards. 7. Score and continue until someone reaches the target score. Enjoy playing Uno!
